best_for: Students, journalists and job seekers building a public data portfolio who are happy for their dashboards and data to be seen by anyone.
description:
Tableau Public is a free platform from Tableau Software for turning public data into visualizations and sharing them online. Tableau calls these vizzes, and you can build them in the free Desktop Public Edition or right in your web browser, with no programming.

Once a viz is on your profile, you can embed it in a web page or blog, or share it by social media or email. Your profile shows how often your vizzes were viewed and favorited, how many people follow you, and who credited your work as inspiration. Turn on the Hire Me button and companies can contact you by email through a form. You can also submit a viz for Viz of the Day.

points.title: Free, and public by design
points.text: Building vizzes costs nothing. Anything you publish to your Tableau Public profile can be opened by anyone online, so keep private or company data out of it.

points.title: Hiding is not privacy
points.text: You can hide a viz from your profile, but anyone with its link can still open it. Visitors can also download a viz and its data by default; switch that off per viz or in your profile settings.

points.title: Local saves are allowed
points.text: The Desktop Public Edition can save workbooks to your computer as well as publish them. It publishes only to Tableau Public, never to Tableau Cloud or Server.

points.title: 15 million rows and file sources
points.text: Each data source is capped at 15M rows, with 10 GB of storage for your content. Connectors are limited to files such as Excel, text, JSON, PDF, spatial and statistical files, plus Google Drive and OData. Data is extracted; live connections are not supported.

points.title: Not for commercial work
points.text: Tableau says the Public Edition is meant for learning and public data, not commercial use. Its Free Edition keeps data private and connects to more sources but cannot publish.

points.title: macOS 13 or later
points.text: Mac packages are built for Intel and Apple Silicon and need macOS 13. Windows gets a 64-bit installer for all users. The Windows listing keeps 11 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
